Quick initial findings from the first 15 mins of collection:
- Symptom: sustained 5xx increase and latency amplification coincident with rising KV cache eviction rates on AZ2.
- Root cause (likely): inference runtime headroom exhausted for long-context requests; KV cache churn + a memory fragmentation pattern in the 2.3.4 runtime build. We see increased GC pauses leading to request timeouts that cascade into queue pile-up.

Immediate mitigations I can implement now (10–20m to flip):
1) Start a phased drain of non-priority traffic from AZ2 -> USW2 (route up to 90% within 15m, keep 10% for canary). Requires routing authorization from ops leadership (sean_gallagher).
2) Trigger automatic fallback to the quantized-4bit variant for Springboard's production model in AZ2/USW2 as a safety net (lower perf but more stable under memory pressure). No config change on their side; we can toggle in the routing layer.
3) Disable aggressive prefix caching for sessions with >1024 tokens for 30 minutes (reduces KV churn); reversible.

Notes on capacity: USW2 has available ephemeral capacity today, but sustained reroute at 90% will increase unit cost and may require a short-term Dedicated warm pool (30–90 days) if traffic persists. That requires a capacity billing commitment; I'll call this out separately.

I recommend doing steps 1+2+3 in that order once we have approval. I'll prepare a runbook snippet and attach the playbook.

-Rishi
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
